concepts.title: Business Transactions, Source Documents and Vouchers

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Business Transactions, Source Documents and Vouchers' refers to.
questions.a: Every business transaction is evidenced by a source document such as a cash memo, invoice, cheque or pay-in-slip, and the accountant prepares an accounting voucher on its basis before the transaction is recorded in the books.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Business Transactions, Source Documents and Vouchers'.
questions.a: Source documents provide the evidence for the entry, and vouchers classify the transaction as debit or credit voucher with a narration.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Business Transactions, Source Documents and Vouchers' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 3.1 Business Transactions and Source Document (source: keac103.txt section 3.1)

concepts.title: Rules of Debit and Credit for Accounts

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Rules of Debit and Credit for Accounts' refers to.
questions.a: Under the modern approach, increases in assets and expenses are debited while decreases are credited; increases in capital, liabilities and incomes are credited while decreases are debited, keeping total debits equal to total credits.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Rules of Debit and Credit for Accounts'.
questions.a: Applying the rules to the affected accounts decides which account is debited and which is credited for any transaction.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Rules of Debit and Credit for Accounts' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 3.3.1 Rules of Debit and Credit (source: keac103.txt section 3.3.1)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Journal, Narration and Compound Entries' refers to.
questions.a: The journal is the book of original entry where transactions are first recorded chronologically with a narration; a compound entry records several debits or credits in one entry, and the process is called journalising.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Journal, Narration and Compound Entries'.
questions.a: The journal entry shows date, accounts, amounts, folio and narration, forming the base for posting into the ledger.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Journal, Narration and Compound Entries' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 3.4 Books of Original Entry (source: keac103.txt journal sections)
